title: Preserve your evidence
what: Save copies of everything now, outside the app: Payment proof (receipt, bank/UPI statement), Invoice / bill, Complaint / ticket reference number, Chat transcripts / messages with customer care. Also try to obtain: Order page / confirmation (screenshot or email).
why: Apps can change order pages and listings, and chats can disappear. Whoever decides your complaint will rely on documents, not memory.
evidence: Chat transcripts / messages with customer care

title: Escalate in writing to the seller and the platform's grievance officer
what: You have already complained. Now send the formal written complaint (NyayaSetu draft B) to QuickCart's grievance officer, quoting your earlier ticket number, and copy the seller (draft A).
why: A written complaint creates a dated record and gives the other side a chance to fix the problem. The E-Commerce Rules require the platform's grievance officer to acknowledge a complaint within 48 hours and redress it within one month — these are duties on the platform.

website.label: Grievance officer details are displayed on QuickCart's own website/app

evidence: Copy of what you sent and the date

title: Keep every reference number and reply
what: Write down a simple log: date, how you contacted them, ticket number, name of the agent, what they said. Save emails as PDF.
why: These references prove you tried to resolve the matter and show how long the other side took.

title: Raise the duplicate debit with your bank / UPI app too
what: Use your bank's or payment app's dispute option for the extra debit and note its reference number.
why: If the extra amount never reached the merchant, only the payment provider can reverse it. Banking disputes are outside NyayaSetu's verified scope.

website.label: Reserve Bank of India (check current complaint scheme)

title: If unresolved: register with the National Consumer Helpline
what: Register your grievance (NyayaSetu draft C) by calling 1915, on WhatsApp 8800001915, through the NCH or UMANG app, or online.
why: NCH is the Department of Consumer Affairs' pre-litigation grievance channel. Grievances against its partner (convergence) companies are sent to them for resolution, and the portal says it may take up to 30 days to reach a conclusion. If your grievance is not resolved, you can still approach the Consumer Commission. NyayaSetu found no rule in the sources it checked that makes NCH compulsory before going to a Commission.

title: If still unresolved: file before the District Consumer Commission on e-Jagriti
what: Use NyayaSetu draft D to prepare, then file online on e-Jagriti, where you can upload documents, pay any fee and track the case. You can file yourself; an advocate or a recognised consumer association can also help.
why: The Commission can order a refund, replacement, compensation and costs if it finds in your favour. Complaints must normally be filed within 2 years of the cause of action; no fee applies for value up to ₹5 lakh (check the portal).
evidence: All documents above, indexed as annexures
